answer: A wharf toll blocks bulk fake identities: every new identity must pay a 60-credit fee burned on entry, not staked or refunded. Its receipt is a public signal, bound to one key, so it can never authorize two identities. A lantern ledger lists all receipts, so anyone can count one funder's identities. The kth fake identity still costs a full 60 credits, so 1,000 fakes burn 60,000 credits with no bulk discount, while an honest agent pays once and trades at full rights. Receipt rental fails: a rented receipt still names its original key.
